title: Pitfalls: common pronunciation and grammar mistakes of English and Dutch speakers

items.title: Third-tone sandhi (你好 is said ní hǎo) and the half-third tone
items.rule: When a 3rd-tone syllable is followed directly by another 3rd tone, the first one is pronounced as a 2nd (rising) tone: 你好 nǐ hǎo is said ní hǎo, 老鼠 lǎoshǔ is said láoshǔ. Before a 1st, 2nd or 4th tone a 3rd tone is pronounced as a 'half-third': low and falling (pitch 21) without the final rise (好吃, 美国, 好看), and a neutral syllable after it is pitched relatively high. Only a 3rd tone said on its own or at the end of a phrase may keep the full dip-and-rise (Wiktionary marks that final rise as optional). With three 3rd tones in a row the grouping decides: 2+1 (展览+馆, 保管+好) makes the first two rise (zhánlánguǎn, báoguán hǎo); 1+2 (老+保管) makes only the middle one rise (lǎo báoguǎn). Pinyin never writes the change: dictionaries and the HSK word list keep nǐ hǎo.
items.details: Rule text: Wikipedia as quoted in pypinyin's ToneSandhiMixin (two 3rd tones, 2+1 and 1+2 groupings, and the caveat that longer chains 'may depend on word boundaries, stress, and dialectal variations'). PaddleSpeech's TTS front end applies the same rules (two 3rd tones: the first becomes 2nd; 蒙古/包 type 2+1: the first two become 2nd; 纸/老虎 type 1+2: only the middle one). Wiktionary IPA (via WikiPron) writes the change as 214→35 and the half-third as 214→21: 你好 ni²¹⁴⁻³⁵ xɑʊ̯²¹⁴⁻²¹⁽⁴⁾; 展覽館 214→35, 214→35, 214→21(4); 我很好 214→35, 214→35, 214→21(4), i.e. wó hén hǎo (the 1+2 grouping rule, 老+保管 → lǎo báoguǎn, would instead give wǒ hén hǎo); half-third before other tones: 好吃 xɑʊ̯²¹⁴⁻²¹ ʈ͡ʂʰʐ̩⁵⁵, 美國 214→21 + 35, 好看 214→21 + 51, 北京, 老師, 考試, 起床, 每天. Neutral syllable after a 3rd tone: 你們 …²¹⁴ mən⁴ (pitch 4, i.e. higher). App convention: keep citation tones in the pinyin field (CC-CEDICT 你好 ni3 hao3; 2025 HSK word list 你好 nǐ hǎo) and show the realised tones in a separate spoken layer.

items.title: 不 bù becomes bú before a 4th tone, and is light in 好不好 / 听不懂
items.rule: 不 is bù (4th tone) on its own and before 1st, 2nd and 3rd tones (不同 bù tóng, 不好意思 bù hǎoyìsi). Before another 4th tone it is pronounced bú: 不是 bú shì, 不要 búyào, 不对 búduì, 不客气 bú kèqi. Between the two halves of an A-不-A question (好不好, 是不是, 贵不贵) and inside potential complements (听不懂, 看不懂; also lexicalised in 对不起 duìbuqǐ) 不 is usually unstressed and toneless: hǎo bu hǎo, tīng bu dǒng.
items.details: Spelling conventions differ, so learners meet both: the 2021 Grading Standards and the 2025 HSK syllabus print the changed tone (不要 búyào, 不用 búyòng, 不错 búcuò, 不但 búdàn, 不客气 bú kèqi; '"一、不"注音时标变调…"不必"标音为"búbì"'), while CC-CEDICT writes bù and only lexicalised neutral forms (对不起 duìbuqǐ, 好不好 hǎo bu hǎo, 听不懂 tīng bu dǒng). This app keeps the CC-CEDICT citation form in 'pinyin' and the pronounced form in 'spoken'. Wiktionary IPA (WikiPron): 不是 pu⁵¹⁻³⁵ ʂʐ̩⁵¹, 不要 pu⁵¹⁻³⁵ jɑʊ̯⁵¹, 不對 pu⁵¹⁻³⁵ tu̯eɪ̯⁵¹, 不客氣 pu⁵¹⁻³⁵ kʰɤ⁵¹ t͡ɕʰi¹; neutral variants 好不好 …b̥u⁴…, 聽不懂 …b̥u²…, 看不懂 …b̥u¹…, 對不起 …b̥u¹…. Examples of A-not-A questions in the 2021 Standards: 这本书贵不贵？ 你吃不吃包子？

items.title: 一 yī: yí before a 4th tone, yì before other tones, yī as a number
items.rule: 一 keeps yī when said alone, when counting or reading out digits (一、二、三; 一零零), as an ordinal (第一 dìyī), at the end of a word (统一 tǒngyī) and in dates (一月 yīyuè 'January', 十一月, 一号 'the 1st'). Before a 4th tone it becomes yí (一个 yí ge, 一样 yíyàng, 一定 yídìng, 一万 yíwàn); before a 1st, 2nd or 3rd tone it becomes yì (一天 yìtiān, 一年 yìnián, 一起 yìqǐ, 一点儿 yìdiǎnr). Between a reduplicated verb it is light and toneless: 看一看 kàn yi kàn, 想一想.
items.details: Rule text: Wikipedia as quoted in pypinyin. PaddleSpeech encodes the same rules: 一 in number sequences unchanged (一零零); ordinal 第一 → yi1; between reduplicated verbs → yi5 (看一看); before tone 4 or a neutral syllable (such as the measure word 个) → yi2 (一段); otherwise yi4 (一天). Wiktionary IPA (WikiPron): 一個 i⁵⁵⁻³⁵ kɤ⁵¹, 一樣 and 一萬 i⁵⁵⁻³⁵, 一千 and 一百 i⁵⁵⁻⁵¹, 一點兒 i⁵⁵⁻⁵¹, 一路平安 i⁵⁵⁻³⁵; unchanged: 一月 i⁵⁵ ɥɛ⁵¹, 一號 i⁵⁵ xɑʊ̯⁵¹, 十一月 …i⁵⁵…, 第一 ti⁵¹ i⁵⁵, 統一 …i⁵⁵. The 2025 HSK word list prints the changed tone (一起 yìqǐ, 一些 yìxiē, 一点儿 yìdiǎnr, 一般 yìbān, 一共 yígòng, 一定 yídìng, 一样 yíyàng, 一半 yíbàn) but 统一 tǒngyī; CC-CEDICT keeps yī everywhere (and notes 一 is also read yāo when spelling out digits). The 2021 Standards use the A一A pattern in 你想一想这个字的意思。

items.title: ü: written u after j, q, x, y — but nǚ ≠ nǔ and lǜ ≠ lù
items.rule: Pinyin ü is the rounded front vowel [y]. After n and l it keeps its two dots, because nu/lu with a plain u are different syllables: 女 nǚ 'woman' vs 努 nǔ, 绿 lǜ 'green' vs 路 lù 'road'. After j, q, x and y the dots are left out (a plain u never occurs there), so ju, qu, xu, yu, jun, quan, xue, yun all contain the ü sound: 居 jū, 去 qù, 虚 xū, 鱼 yú, 军 jūn, 云 yún. Every other pinyin u is [u] (不 bù, 路 lù). Dutch speakers already have [y]: it is Dutch uu (vuur, minuut; Dutch 'nu' [ny] sounds like 女 nǚ) and German ü (über, für). English has no such vowel: it combines the tongue position of 'ee' [i] with the lip rounding of 'oo' [u].
items.details: Spelling rule from 《汉语拼音方案》 (quoted in the pypinyin docs). CC-CEDICT's syllable inventory confirms it: ü (written u: in CC-CEDICT) only appears as nü, nüe, lü, lüe; with j, q, x, y it is always spelled ju, juan, jue, jun, qu…, yu, yuan, yue, yun, and j/q/x are never followed by anything but i or ü. Wiktionary IPA (WikiPron cmn): 女 ny²¹⁴ vs 努 nu²¹⁴; 綠 ly⁵¹ vs 路 lu⁵¹; 去 t͡ɕʰy⁵¹; 居 t͡ɕy⁵⁵; 區 t͡ɕʰy⁵⁵; 虛 ɕy⁵⁵; 魚 y³⁵; 雨 y²¹⁴; 雲 yn³⁵; 軍 t͡ɕyn⁵⁵; 學 ɕy̯ɛ³⁵. Dutch (WikiPron nld): vuur vyr, minuut minyt, muur myr, nu ny, u y — but Dutch short u is [ʏ] (dun dʏn, bus bʏs) and Dutch oe is [u] (boek buk, doen dun), which is the value of ordinary pinyin u. German (WikiPron deu): über yːbɐ, für fyːr, Tür tyːr, müde myːdə.

items.title: zh ch sh r vs z c s vs j q x (and the 'i' in shi / si)
items.rule: Mandarin has three series of hissing/hushing initials. Retroflex zh [ʈʂ], ch [ʈʂʰ], sh [ʂ], r [ʐ] are made with the tongue tip raised toward the roof of the mouth (中 zhōng, 吃 chī, 是 shì, 日 rì, 热 rè). Dental z [ts], c [tsʰ], s [s] are made at the teeth (字 zì, 次 cì, 四 sì). Alveolo-palatal j [tɕ], q [tɕʰ], x [ɕ] are made with the tongue body raised to the hard palate, between English 's' and 'sh' (鸡 jī, 七 qī, 西 xī), and occur only before i or ü. So z is a 'ts' and never a voiced z, c is a 'ts' with a puff of air, q is not 'kw' and x is not 'ks'. After z/c/s and zh/ch/sh/r the letter i is not 'ee' but a buzzing continuation of the consonant: 四 sì [sz̩], 是 shì [ʂʐ̩] — so 是 shì, 十 shí, 四 sì and 西 xī are four different syllables.
items.details: Initials of 《汉语拼音方案》 (via pypinyin docs): b p m f d t n l g k h j q x zh ch sh r z c s. IPA from Wiktionary via WikiPron: 中 ʈ͡ʂʊŋ, 吃 ʈ͡ʂʰʐ̩, 是 ʂʐ̩, 十 ʂʐ̩, 日 ʐ̩, 熱 ʐɤ; 字 t͡sz̩, 次 t͡sʰz̩, 四 sz̩, 資 t͡sz̩; 雞 t͡ɕi, 七 t͡ɕʰi, 西 ɕi, 去 t͡ɕʰy. CC-CEDICT syllable inventory: the only i-syllables after these initials are zi, ci, si, zhi, chi, shi, ri; j/q/x are only followed by i or ü (written u). For comparison, English ch/sh/j are palato-alveolar (WikiPron eng: cheese t͡ʃiz, she ʃi, jeep d͡ʒiːp) — a fourth place that matches none of the Mandarin series exactly — and English/Dutch z is voiced [z] (zoo zuː; Dutch zee zeː, zon zɔn).

items.title: Vowels that don't sound like they look: e, ian, ui, iu, un, ong
items.rule: Pinyin e on its own or after a consonant is [ɤ], an unrounded 'uh' made far back in the mouth (喝 hē, 哥 gē, 热 rè, 饿 è); but e is [ɛ] in ie and üe (谢 xiè, 月 yuè), [e] in ei and ui, and [ə] in en (很 hěn). ian sounds like 'yen' [i̯ɛn] (天 tiān, 件 jiàn), not 'yan'. Three spellings are abbreviations with a hidden vowel: iu = iou (牛 niú [ni̯oʊ̯]), ui = uei (对 duì [tu̯eɪ̯], 水 shuǐ), un = uen (论 lùn [lu̯ən]) — except after j, q, x, y, where un stands for ün (军 jūn, 云 yún). ong is [ʊŋ] with a rounded vowel close to 'oo' (东 dōng, 中 zhōng).

items.title: b/p, d/t, g/k: the difference is a puff of air, not voicing
items.rule: The pairs b–p, d–t, g–k, z–c, zh–ch, j–q differ in aspiration. The second of each pair is released with a clear puff of air (p [pʰ], t [tʰ], k [kʰ], c [tsʰ], ch [ʈʂʰ], q [tɕʰ]); the first has no puff and is voiceless: b [p], d [t], g [k], z [ts], zh [ʈʂ], j [tɕ]. English speakers already puff word-initial p/t/k (pin, tea, cat), which is right for pinyin p/t/k; for b/d/g they should neither voice nor puff. Dutch speakers: Dutch b and d are voiced and Dutch p/t/k have no puff, so a Dutch p/t/k is a good model for pinyin b/d/g, while pinyin p/t/k/c/ch/q need an extra puff of air. Never use the Dutch fricative g for pinyin g, which is [k].

items.title: Dutch spelling habits that mislead in pinyin (u/oe/uu, j, g, h, w, z, ui, ie, ou)
items.rule: Read pinyin letters with pinyin values, not Dutch ones: u = Dutch oe [u] (不 bù, 路 lù), except after j/q/x/y and ü, where it is Dutch uu [y] (女 nǚ ≈ Dutch 'nu'); j = [tɕ] (鸡 jī), never Dutch j [j]; g = [k] without a puff (哥 gē), never the Dutch fricative g; h = [x], i.e. the Dutch ch of lachen/acht (好 hǎo), not Dutch h; w = an English-type [w] (我 wǒ), not the Dutch labiodental w; z = [ts] (字 zì), not Dutch z; ui = [u̯eɪ̯] (对 duì), not Dutch ui; ie = [i̯ɛ] (谢 xiè), not Dutch ie [i]; ou = [oʊ̯] (有 yǒu), not Dutch ou [ɑu̯].
items.details: Side-by-side IPA from Wiktionary via WikiPron. Mandarin (cmn): 不 pu, 路 lu, 女 ny, 雞 t͡ɕi, 哥 kɤ, 好 xɑʊ̯, 我 wɔ, 字 t͡sz̩, 對 tu̯eɪ̯, 謝 ɕi̯ɛ, 有 joʊ̯. Dutch (nld): boek buk, doen dun (oe = [u]); vuur vyr, nu ny (uu/u = [y]); ja jaː (j = [j]); goed ɣut (g = [ɣ]); lachen lɑxə, acht ɑxt (ch = [x]); huis ɦœy̯s, hoed ɦut (h = [ɦ]); wat ʋɑt, water ʋaːtər (w = [ʋ]); zee zeː (z = [z]); uit œy̯t (ui = [œy̯]); ziek zik, tien tin (ie = [i]); oud ɑu̯t, jou jɑu̯ (ou = [ɑu̯]). The same IPA symbol in both lists means a close enough sound for a learner; vowel length and fine tongue position still differ.

items.title: Neutral tone: particles and toneless second syllables (东西 dōngxi vs dōngxī)
items.rule: Some syllables have no tone of their own: they are short and light, and their pitch depends on the syllable before (half-low after a 1st tone, mid after a 2nd, higher after a 3rd, lowest after a 4th). Pinyin writes them without a tone mark (包子 bāozi). The neutral tone is obligatory for grammatical particles — 的/地/得 de, 了 le, 吗 ma, 呢 ne, 吧 ba, aspect 着 zhe and 过 guo — for suffixes such as -们 and -子, for reduplicated kinship terms and verbs (妈妈, 奶奶, 试试), and for the second syllable of many everyday words (谢谢 xièxie, 朋友 péngyou, 喜欢 xǐhuan, 先生 xiānsheng, 衣服 yīfu, 时候 shíhou, 名字 míngzi, 认识 rènshi, 休息 xiūxi, 客气 kèqi). It can distinguish words: 东西 dōngxi 'thing, stuff' vs 东西 dōngxī 'east and west'.
items.details: Official notation (2021 Grading Standards): '必读轻声的音节不标声调，如"包子"标音为"bāozi"'. The 2025 HSK word list prints 东西 dōngxi, 谢谢 xièxie, 朋友 péngyou, 喜欢 xǐhuan, 先生 xiānsheng, 衣服 yīfu, 时候 shíhou, 名字 míngzi, 认识 rènshi, 休息 xiūxi and the particles 了 le, 的 de, 得 de, 地 de, 吗 ma, 呢 ne, 吧 ba. CC-CEDICT: 东西 [dong1 xi1] 'east and west' vs [dong1 xi5] 'thing; stuff; person'. PaddleSpeech's TTS front end makes sentence-final 吧/呢/啊…, word-final 的/地/得, aspect 了/着/过, the suffixes 们/子 and reduplicated nouns/verbs (奶奶, 试试) neutral, and lists 东西, 朋友, 喜欢, 先生, 衣服, 时候, 名字, 认识, 休息, 客气 among its 'must neutral tone' words. Pitch of the neutral syllable (Wiktionary IPA via WikiPron): 包子 …⁵⁵ + ², 朋友 …³⁵ + ³, 你們 …²¹⁴ + ⁴, 謝謝 …⁵¹ + ¹.

items.title: 了 is not a past-tense marker
items.rule: 了 marks aspect, not tense. Verb + 了 (了1) presents an action as completed, typically with a counted object: 他买了一本书. Sentence-final 了 (了2) signals a change of state or a new situation: 我累了, 下雨了, 她病了 — and works for the future too: 要下雨了 'it's going to rain', 我们快要放假了. A past event is negated with 没(有) + verb and no 了: 他没买书, 他没吃早饭 (not *他没买了书). Past states, and past events whose time or manner is in focus with 是…的 or 才, usually take no 了 (当时我很讨厌爸爸; 我是昨天到北京的; 我今天八点才起床).
items.details: 2021 Grading Standards: 【一 21】动态助词：了1 — 他买了一本书。／他没买书。我写了两个汉字。／我没写汉字。; 【一 40】变化态 (了2) — 她病了。／她没病。雨小了。／雨没小。他吃早饭了。／他没吃早饭。; 【一 41】完成态 — 他买了两个面包。／他没买面包。; 【一 31】下雨了。; 【二 81】要／快要／就要……了 — 要下雨了。我们快要放假了。; 【二 60】是……的 — 我是昨天到北京的。; 【二 20】才 — 我今天八点才起床。 CC-CEDICT 了 [le5]: '(completed action marker); (modal particle indicating change of state, situation now)'. Learner corpora: YACLC '当时，我不明白我父亲的想法，很讨厌爸爸了。' corrected to '…很讨厌爸爸。'; MuCGEC '…我没学了新的东西。' corrected to '…我没学到新的东西' / '…我没学新的东西'.

items.title: 不 vs 没(有): 'not' vs 'didn't / doesn't have'
items.rule: 不 negates what is or will be the case — states, adjectives, habits, intentions and future actions: 今天不热, 他不去医院 'he isn't going to the hospital'. 没 or 没有 negates that something happened (past or completed actions), without 了: 他昨天没上课, 我今天没有吃早饭. 有 'to have / there is' is only ever negated with 没: 他没有哥哥, 房间里没有桌子 (never *不有).
items.details: 2021 Grading Standards: 【一 14】否定副词：别、不、没、没有 — 今天不热。他昨天没上课。我今天没有吃早饭。; 【一 29】他不去医院。; 【一 37】"有"字句 — 我有很多书。他没有哥哥。房间里没有桌子。; 【一 40】他吃早饭了。／他没吃早饭。 CC-CEDICT: 没 [mei2] '(negative prefix for verbs) have not; not'; 没有 [mei2 you3] 'haven't; hasn't; doesn't exist; to not have; to not be'; 不 [bu4] 'no; not so; (bound form) not; un-'. A related learner error (MuCGEC): '吸烟虽然对健康不有利' corrected to '…对健康不利'.

items.title: Number + measure word + noun (一个人, 两本书)
items.rule: A number, or 这/那/哪/几/每, cannot attach directly to a noun: a measure word (classifier) goes in between — 两本书 'two books', 一件衣服 'a piece of clothing', 那个书包 'that schoolbag', 三口人 'three people (in a family)'. 个 is the general measure word for people and for nouns without a special one, and is usually toneless after a number (一个 yí ge, 两个 liǎng ge). Common specific ones: 本 books; 张 flat things such as paper and tables; 杯 a cup/glass of; 位 people (polite); 只 many animals and one of a pair; 件 clothes and matters; 条 long thin things (rivers, roads, trousers) and dogs; 辆 vehicles. 个 can stand in for some specific measure words, so it is the safe default, but 本/杯/位/张 are expected with their nouns.
items.details: 2021 Grading Standards: 【一 08】名量词：杯、本、个、家、间、口、块、页 — 两杯牛奶 三本书 四个学生 五家商店 六间房子 三口人 七块面包; 【二 10】名量词：层、封、件、条、位 — 两层楼 一封信 一件衣服 一条河 一位老师; 【一 23】数量短语 — 一个 两杯 三本 四包 五块; 【一 06】— 她喜欢那个书包。 2025 HSK grammar syllabus: HSK1 专用名量词 本、个、家、口、块、件、只、元 and 借用名量词 杯; HSK2 条、位、间、名; HSK3 把、双、张、种、层、封、页、辆…. CC-CEDICT: 个 '(classifier used before a noun that has no specific classifier)'; 本 'classifier for books, periodicals, files etc'; 张 'classifier for flat objects, sheet'; 杯 'classifier for certain containers of liquids: glass, cup'; 位 'classifier for people (honorific)'; 只 'classifier for birds and certain animals, one of a pair, some utensils…'; 件 'classifier for events, things, clothes etc'; 条 'classifier for long thin things (ribbon, river, road, trousers etc)'; 辆 'classifier for vehicles'; noun entries: 书 CL:本, 车 CL:辆, 纸 CL:张, 桌子 CL:张, 衣服 CL:件, 狗 CL:只/条, 裤子 CL:条, 老师 CL:个/位, 咖啡 CL:杯. 新华字典 个: '用于没有专用量词的事物…也可用于某些有专用量词的事物'. Toneless 个 after numerals: CC-CEDICT 一个 [yi1 ge5]; PaddleSpeech '个做量词' → neutral.

items.title: 的, 地, 得: three particles, one sound (de)
items.rule: As particles all three are pronounced de with a neutral tone, so the difference shows in writing (chat messages, email): 的 comes before a noun (modifier + 的 + noun: 你的衣服, 干净的房间); 地 comes before a verb (adverbial + 地 + verb: 高兴地说 'said happily'); 得 comes after a verb or adjective and introduces a complement of degree or possibility (跑得很快 'runs fast', 听得懂 'can understand'). Quick test: …的 + noun, …地 + verb, verb + 得 + …
items.details: 2021 Grading Standards: 【一 20】结构助词：的1、地 — 你的衣服很好看。他高兴地说："我明天回家。"; 【一 27】我喜欢干净的房间。; 【二 31】结构助词：得 — 他走得有点儿快。她篮球打得很不错。; 【二 51】状态补语 — 她跑得很快。我们玩儿得很高兴。; 【三 48】可能补语 — 老师的话我都听得懂。 2025 HSK word list: 的 de 助 (HSK1); 得 de 助 and 地 de 助 (HSK2), while 得 dé 'to get' and 地 dì 'ground' (HSK3) keep full tones. CC-CEDICT: 的 [de5] '(used after an attribute when it modifies a noun)'; 地 [de5] '-ly; structural particle: used before a verb or adjective, linking it to preceding modifying adverbial adjunct'; 得 [de5] 'structural particle: used after a verb (or adjective as main verb), linking it to following phrase indicating effect, degree, possibility etc'. Learner errors: MuCGEC '有的孩子从小就开始拼命的学习。' → '…拼命地学习。'; YACLC '这个星期的时间过的很愉快' → '…过得很愉快'; YACLC '跟他们的相处的更愉快' → '跟他们相处得更愉快'. Automatic pinyin can get this wrong too: the pinyin-pro library used as a second opinion by check.mjs reads 高兴地 as dì and 跑得很快 as dé.

examples.english: Your clothes look nice. (的 + noun)

items.title: 二 èr vs 两 liǎng
items.rule: Both mean 'two'. Use 两 before a measure word (两个人, 两本书, 两杯) and for clock time (两点 2:00 — but 两点二十五 2:25 and 十二点 12:00); 两 is also usual before 千, 万, 亿 (两千, 两万). Use 二 when counting or naming the number (一、二、三), for the tens and units of a larger number (十二, 二十, 一千三百五十二, 二十位学生), in ordinals (第二, 二楼 'second floor', 二月 'February') and in decimals and fractions (零点二四, 五分之二). Before 百 both occur (二百, 两百). With traditional weights both work (两斤 or 二斤), but two of the unit 两 is always 二两. When a number is read out digit by digit (phone, room or bus numbers), 1 is often said yāo (幺) for clarity.
items.details: 新华字典, entry 两: '一般用在量词或"半、千、万、亿"等前面…在多位数中常是大数用"两"，小数用"二"（"两"和"二"也可通用）'; '⑴有的数目字只能用"二"不能用"两"，如一、二、三，二十等中的"二"；⑵小数和分数只能用"二"…如零点二四（0.24），五分之二等；⑶序数也只能用"二"…如二姐，第二名等'; '③在传统的度量衡单位前，"两"和"二"可通用 两斤（二斤）。但"二两"不能用成"两两"。④新的度量衡单位前，一般用"两" 两米、两吨'. 2021 Grading Standards: 【一 07】数词 — 十二 二十 二百 两百 / 两个人 两本书; 【一 44】钟点 — 两点 (2:00), 两点二十五（分）, 差两分八点; 【二 09】— 一千三百五十二, 两万一千四百六十五; 【二 72】序数 — 第一 第三 第七 二楼 三层; other examples: 我们班由两位老师和二十位学生组成。都十二点了。机票差不多要两千块钱。卡里只有二百块钱。 Wiktionary (WikiPron) has 二月 ˀɤɻ⁵¹⁻⁵³ ɥɛ⁵¹ and 第二. items.title: 会, 能, 可以: three words for 'can'
items.rule: 会 = know how to (a learned skill: 我不会说中文, 他一句中文也不会说) and also 'will, be likely to' in predictions (他病了，今天大概不会来上课了; 我今年也许会去中国学习中文). 能 = be able to / be in a position to, when ability or circumstances decide (明天你能来吗? 'can you make it tomorrow?'); 不能 often means 'must not / you can't' (筷子不能那样拿). 可以 = may, be allowed to (老师，我可以进来吗? 这儿不可以停车). Requests and permission overlap: both 能 and 可以 are used (我能用用你的手机吗? 你能再给我发一下儿吗?). For a learned skill the default is 会.
items.details: CC-CEDICT: 会 [hui4] 'can; to have the skill; to know how to; to be likely to; to be sure to'; 能 [neng2] 'can; to be able to; might possibly'; 可以 [ke3 yi3] 'can; may; possible; able to'. 新华字典 会 ⒋ '能，可能，善于 共产主义一定会实现。他会开飞机。' 2021 Grading Standards: 【一 02】能愿动词：会、能 — 我不会说中文。明天你能来吗？; 【二 01】能愿动词 (1) 可能 (2) 可以 — 老师，我可以进来吗？这儿不可以停车。; 【二 04】我能用用你的手机吗？; 【二 07】筷子不能那样拿。; 【二 19】我今年也许会去中国学习中文。; level 3: 他病了，今天大概不会来上课了。他一句中文也不会说。你的文件我打不开，你能再给我发一下儿吗？ The 2025 HSK grammar syllabus lists 会、能、想、要、可以 as HSK1 modal verbs. Learner error (YACLC): '我希望早就修理，要不然我不会洗澡啊。' corrected to '…要不然我不能洗澡啊。' — the problem was a broken shower (circumstance), not a missing skill. (Example sentence 我不会说中文 is not used below because the checker's segmentation reads 说中 as one word.)

items.title: 您们 is not the polite plural: use 大家, 各位 or 你们
items.rule: 您 nín is the polite singular 'you'. The Xinhua Dictionary advises against adding 们: for more than one person say 您俩 or 您二位 (two), 您仨 or 您三位 (three), 您诸位 (more). In everyday speech a group is addressed as 你们, 大家 'everyone' or 各位 'everybody, ladies and gentlemen' (各位朋友，下午好!). 您们 is missing from CC-CEDICT and from the HSK pronoun lists (which contain 您 but not 您们), although the form exists (Wiktionary has an entry) and you may see it written.
items.details: 新华字典 您: '注意用于多数时不加词尾"们"，两个人称"您俩"或"您二位"，三个人称"您仨"或"您三位"，三个人以上称"您诸位"。' CC-CEDICT: no entry 您们; 您 'you (courteous, as opposed to informal 你)'; 各位 'everybody; all (guests, colleagues etc); all of you'; 大家 'everyone'. 2025 HSK grammar syllabus HSK1 人称代词: 我、你、您、他、她、我们、你们、他们、她们、它、它们、大家; 各位 is an HSK4 word (and an HSK3 指示代词 in the 2021 Standards: 各位朋友，下午好！). WikiPron lists a Wiktionary entry 您們 (nín + men). A learner wrote '…非常麻烦您们了,谢谢您.' (YACLC); one annotator corrected it to '麻烦你们了,谢谢你们！' while another left 您们 — usage is not uniform, but standard references avoid it.

items.title: Replying to 谢谢: 不客气, 不用谢, 没事 — 没关系 answers an apology
items.rule: Answer thanks with 不客气 (bú kèqi, literally 'don't be polite'), 不用谢 ('no need to thank me') or 不用客气; casually also 没事(儿) ('it's nothing'). 没关系 means 'it doesn't matter' and is the reply to an apology (对不起 → 没关系), not to thanks; 没事 fits both. Note that 不客气 also has an ordinary meaning 'impolite, blunt' when it describes how someone behaves.
items.details: CC-CEDICT: 不客气 'you're welcome; don't mention it; impolite; rude; blunt'; 不用谢 'You're welcome; Don't mention it'; 不用客气 'you're welcome; don't mention it; no need to stand on ceremony'; 没事 'it's not important; it's nothing; never mind; to have nothing to do; to be free; to be all right'; 没事儿 '…it's not important; it's nothing; never mind'; 没关系 'it doesn't matter'. 2025 HSK syllabus: 谢谢 xièxie, 不客气 bú kèqi, 没关系 méi guānxi, 没事 méishì and 对不起 duìbuqǐ are all HSK1 words, and the HSK1 task list asks learners to exchange simple courtesies '如你好、谢谢、对不起、再见等'. The 2021 Standards use 没事儿 in '他笑着说："没事儿。"'. Whether 不客气 sounds stiffer than 不用谢 / 没事 in today's mainland speech was not verified (see open questions).

items.title: 对不起 vs 不好意思 vs 抱歉; 打扰一下 / 请问 for 'excuse me'
items.rule: 对不起 is a real apology ('I'm sorry; I let you down'), for an actual fault — e.g. after being told you broke a rule. 不好意思 is lighter ('sorry — I'm embarrassed to trouble you'): small lapses, inconveniencing someone, interrupting, asking a favour (不好意思，我没拿来). 抱歉 'sorry' is more formal, e.g. staff speaking to a customer (抱歉，先生，这里禁止吸烟). To get attention or interrupt, use 打扰一下 ('sorry to bother you') or 请问 ('may I ask…'). 劳驾 'excuse me' also exists but the 2025 HSK syllabus places it in the advanced 7–9 band.
items.details: CC-CEDICT: 对不起 'I'm sorry; excuse me; I beg your pardon; to let (sb) down; to disappoint'; 不好意思 'to feel embarrassed; to find it embarrassing; to be sorry (for inconveniencing sb)'; 抱歉 'to be sorry; to feel apologetic; sorry!'; 打扰 'to disturb; to bother; to trouble'; 请问 'Excuse me, may I ask...?'; 劳驾 'excuse me'. 2025 HSK syllabus levels: 对不起 and 请问 HSK1; 不好意思 HSK2; 抱歉 and 打扰 HSK4; 劳驾 HSK7–9. Official sample listening dialogue: '女：抱歉，先生，这里禁止吸烟。男：对不起，我马上离开。这附近哪里能吸烟？' Official sample reading item: '（打扰）一下，同学，请不要在自习室里大声讨论。' 2021 Standards 【二 50】: '甲：你的词典呢？乙：不好意思，我没拿来。'

items.title: No 是 before adjectives: 我很忙, not *我是忙
items.rule: Chinese adjectives are predicates by themselves, so there is no 'to be' before them: 我很忙 'I'm busy', 房间很干净 'the room is clean', 今天不冷 'it isn't cold today'. 是 links a subject to a noun (他是我的老师). In a plain positive statement the adjective normally takes a degree adverb — usually 很, which here often does not mean 'very' — or 非常, 太…了, 最, or is negated with 不. 是 + adjective + 的 is a different pattern that classifies (花是白的 'the flowers are white ones').
items.details: CC-CEDICT: 是 'to be (followed by substantives only)'; 很 'very; quite; (also, often used before an adjective without intensifying its meaning, i.e. as a meaningless syntactic element)'. 2021 Grading Standards: 【一 30】形容词谓语句 — 房间很干净。这个学生最认真。; 【一 25】今天不冷。这个菜很好吃。; 【一 05】她很高。; 【一 36】"是"字句 (1) 他是我的老师。(2) 表示说明或特征 — 花是白的。衣服是干净的。 Learner corpora: YACLC '她也是很苗条' → '她很苗条'; MuCGEC '这是很有意思。' → '这很有意思。'; YACLC '去关西大学半路上的马路上拥挤。' → '…马路上很拥挤。' (annotators added 很 to a bare adjective).

examples.english: The room is clean. (adjective predicate with 很, no 是)

items.title: 比 comparisons take no 很
items.rule: In A 比 B + adjective the adjective stands on its own: 我朋友比我高 'my friend is taller than me'. To say 'even more' use 更 or 还 before the adjective (他的手机比我的更贵; 今天比昨天还凉快); to say by how much, put the amount after the adjective (姐姐比我大两岁; 房间外边比里边凉快一些). Do not add 很 (*花钱比赚钱很少).
items.details: 2021 Grading Standards: 【一 38】比较句1 (1) A比B＋形容词 — 我朋友比我高。这个手机比那个贵。(2) A没有B＋形容词 — 昨天没有今天热。; 【二 58】比较句2 (1) A比B＋形容词＋数量补语 — 姐姐比我大两岁。房间外边比里边凉快一些。(2) A比B＋更／还＋形容词 — 他的手机比我的更贵。今天比昨天还凉快。 None of the official 比 patterns contains 很. Learner corpus (YACLC): '最重要的是花钱比赚钱很少。' → '最重要的是花钱比赚钱少。'; '明天可能复习比今天的复习很好。' → '明天可能复习得比今天更好。'

items.title: Question words stay in place, and no 吗 with them
items.rule: For a wh-question keep statement order and put the question word in the slot where the answer will go: 你买什么? — 我买一个面包; 你们去哪儿?; 谁是老师?; 你怎么去医院? There is no inversion and no 'do'. 吗 turns a statement into a yes/no question (他是老师吗?) and is not added to a question that already has 什么, 哪儿, 谁, 怎么, 几 and so on. (Question words can also be indefinite 'somewhere/something': 我好像在哪儿见过你 'I think I've seen you somewhere'.)
items.details: 2021 Grading Standards: 【一 04】疑问代词 — 你们去哪儿？你买什么？谁是老师？你怎么去医院？车站在哪里？; 【一 29】我买一个面包。; 【一 33】(1) 是非问句 他是老师吗？ (2) 特指问句 谁跟你一起去书店？你想买什么？; 【一 45】用"吗"提问 — 他是老师吗？这包子好吃吗？; 【一 46】我们在哪儿见面？你星期天做什么？; 【三 07】不定指用法 — 我好像在哪儿见过你。 CC-CEDICT 吗 [ma5]: '(question particle for "yes-no" questions)'; 什么 'what?; something; anything'. 哪儿 and 哪里 are both standard (both are in the HSK1 question-word list).

items.title: Time and place go before the verb
items.rule: Basic order is Subject – Time – Place – Verb – Object: 我每天在家学习 'I study at home every day' (and in the same way 我明天在家工作 'I'm working from home tomorrow'). Time words (今天, 明天, 每天, 十点, 下午) go before the verb, after the subject or at the very start (他十点睡觉; 明天下雨，我们在家休息). A place phrase with 在 also comes before the verb (哥哥在北京学中文; 她在网上买了两本书). English and Dutch put both after the verb ('I work at home tomorrow', 'Ik werk morgen thuis'). Exception: with verbs of putting and placing, 在 + place after the verb gives where the thing ends up (这些书不能放在外边).
items.details: 2021 Grading Standards: 【一 28】状语 — 表示时间、处所的词语作状语: 他十点睡觉。我们下午去吧。她在网上买了两本书。; 【一 15】我们从星期一到星期五工作。; 【一 16】在 — 哥哥在北京学中文。他在手机上看电影。; 【二 66】明天下雨，我们在家休息。; 【五 33】多项状语 — 他昨天在教室里认真地写完了作业。她为了通过考试昨天在家复习了一整天。 (time, place, manner, then the verb); 【三 47】example 这些书不能放在外边，应该拿进去。 2025 HSK grammar syllabus HSK1: 状语 '表示时间、处所的词语作状语'. Learner corpus (YACLC): '每天我学习在家，我做作业，写汉字，复习旧课词语。' corrected to '每天我在家学习，…' / '我每天在家学习，…'. 我明天在家工作 is a slot variant (明天, 工作) of the corrected sentence.

items.title: 和 joins nouns, not sentences
items.rule: 和 (and 跟) means 'and' between nouns or noun phrases: 我和弟弟都学习中文, 爸爸跟妈妈都不在家. It is not used to join two clauses the way English 'and' is: 我喜欢看电视，弟弟喜欢打球 needs no connector (or use 也, 还, 而且, 然后 as the meaning requires). In lists, separate the items with the enumeration comma 、 and put 和 before the last item without a comma: 北京、台北、香港、澳门和成都.
items.details: 2021 Grading Standards: 【一 19】连接词或短语：跟2、还是、和2 — 爸爸跟妈妈都不在家。我和弟弟都学习中文。; 【一 39】并列复句 (1) 不用关联词语 — 我喜欢看电视，弟弟喜欢打球。(2) ……，也…… — 我喜欢唱歌，弟弟也喜欢唱歌。 The 2025 HSK grammar syllabus classifies 和2 under '连接词语或短语' and lists clause connectors separately ('连接分句或者句子：但、但是、那、虽然、还是2、因为2、所以'; HSK3 adds 不但、而且、如果、可是、然后). Learner corpora: MuCGEC '我觉得我们每个人都应该进自己的责任，和不浪费能源。' corrected to '…尽自己的责任，不浪费能源。'; YACLC '北京，台北，香港，澳门，和成都' corrected to '北京、台北、香港、澳门和成都'.

items.title: 也 and 都 go after the subject, right before the verb
items.rule: 也 'also, too' and 都 'all, both' are adverbs: they come after the subject and before the verb (or before 是, 很, 不): 他是学生，我也是学生 'he's a student and so am I'; 同学们都很认真; 爸爸跟妈妈都不在家. They never open a sentence the way English 'Also, …' does (*也他比我强 → 他也比我强), and 都 sums up the people or things named before it.
items.details: 2021 Grading Standards: 【一 13】关联副词：还1、也 — 他是学生，我也是学生。; 【一 10】范围、协同副词：都1 — 同学们都很认真。; 【一 19】爸爸跟妈妈都不在家。我和弟弟都学习中文。; 【一 39】我喜欢唱歌，弟弟也喜欢唱歌。 2025 HSK grammar syllabus HSK1: 范围副词 都1; 关联副词 还1、也. Learner corpus (MuCGEC): '但是他比我高，也他比我强' corrected to '…他也比我强' / '…也比我强'; YACLC '联明天也我们都不知道…' corrected to '连明天我们都不知道…'.
